summary: Macro backdrop for ags: mixed (score +0 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china 0; breadth 0. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Class III milk +17.1%; weakest: Oats -17.2%. Key releases ahead: US Federal Funds Rate (10-28 2:00 PM ET); US FOMC Statement (10-28 2:00 PM ET); US FOMC Press Conference (10-28 2:30 PM ET); US Advance GDP q/q (10-29 8:30 AM ET); US Core PCE Price Index m/m (10-29 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.05% (-19 bp in a month), 2-year 4.67% (-25 bp); 2s10s curve +38 bp (+6 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.00% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 102.14 (+0.9% in a month, +3.9% YTD). USD/BRL 5.348 (+3.1% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.665 (-0.7%); USD/MXN 18.62 (+4.9%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 +0.8% in a month (+13.1% YTD); VIX 16.9. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 101.92 $/bbl (+14.5% in a month), Brent 110.46, ULSD 4.634 $/gal (+6.1%), natural gas 3.03 (-12.2%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper +0.7% in a month, Shanghai Composite -3.7%, Hang Seng -6.3%, yuan +0.7% vs USD. Mixed China signals.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 13 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (39%); S&P GSCI +3.1% in a month; gold -2.1%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
